9.0.s.en: (1) God is the One who destroys the pagans

9.0.0.en: Fenced up to heaven: a figure for the height of the cities' walls and the difficulty of getting past them.

9.0.1.en: The sons of Anak: they lived in the south of Palestine, between Jerusalem and Hebron, and were described as giants because of their great stature and their strength in war.

9.0.2.en: God announces to them that they will cross the Jordan River, enter and possess the land of Canaan, which is inhabited by a people of giants who live in fortified cities, the sons of Anak, of whom all the peoples are afraid.

9.1.0.en: A consuming fire: a destroying power.

9.1.1.en: He draws their attention to the great power of God, which He likens to a consuming fire that will pass before them, frightening the enemies and supporting His children, so that they will easily be able to overcome their enemies. The secret of the strength of God's people is God's presence with them.

9.1.2.en: May you attribute every success you achieve to God; rather, let God's grace grow great in your eyes, because it works in your weakness and your difficult circumstances. In this way your faith is made firm and the work of God's power in you increases.

9.2.0.en: God warns them not to attribute their victory over their enemies to their own righteousness and the wickedness of the enemies. It is God, who is tender toward His people, who gave them this righteousness and forgave them their sins, so they must thank God for His grace toward them and must not be proud.

9.3.0.en: The victory of God's people did not come because of their righteousness and the uprightness of their conduct, but the reasons for this victory are:

9.3.1.en: 1- The wickedness of the enemies in worshiping idols and in evil lusts.

9.3.2.en: 2- God's promises to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

9.4.0.en: Stiffnecked: a figurative expression meaning stubborn, resistant and disobedient.

9.4.1.en: So that God's people would not be proud, He reminds them of their stubbornness and their rebellion against Him, yet God in His longsuffering bears with them and calls them to repentance. Because they believe in Him, they return to Him. In sum, they fall into evil like the enemies, but what distinguishes them is their faith in God and His power working in them.

9.5.s.en: (2) Examples of the disobedience of God's people

9.5.0.en: You provoked the Lord to wrath: you made the Lord angry.

9.5.1.en: God draws their attention to the repetition of their disobedience toward Him: they stirred up His anger against them many times throughout their journey in the wilderness of Sinai.

9.6.0.en: He reminds them of their worship of the golden calf at Horeb (Ex 32:4); God was angry with them and wanted to destroy them, and many of them were killed by the hand of Moses.

9.7.0.en: He reminds them of the incident of the golden calf, when Moses went up the mountain to receive the Ten Commandments written on two tables of stone, and fasted there forty days, and received them from God (Ex 32). They are the very same words that God spoke when He appeared on the mountain in the form of a great fire (Ex 19, 20).

9.8.0.en: At the end of the forty days and forty nights the Lord said to him, "Arise, get thee down quickly," for the people had transgressed the commandment and had made a golden image of a calf and worshiped it.

9.9.0.en: Let me alone, that I may destroy them: perhaps Moses bowed down before God and began to intercede for his people. This also shows the standing of Moses and of the people with God.

9.9.1.en: The Lord wanted to destroy the people as a recompense for their disobedience to the commandment and their rebellion against Him, and it became perfectly clear that they were a stubborn and resistant people. He asked Moses not to hold on to them, for He would utterly put an end to them as a nation, and from the descendants of Moses another people, better than they, would arise. Then Moses came down from the mountain with the two tables of the covenant in his hands.

9.10.0.en: When Moses saw the people's abandonment of God and their worship of the golden calf, he was very angry and cast down the tables of the Law, and they were broken.

9.11.0.en: As at the first: that is, as he pleaded for them the first time, when the Lord commanded him to go down and see the people, who had made themselves a molten image (Ex 32:11). Moses fell down before the Lord, fasting, forty days and forty nights again, as before, pleading before the Lord to forgive the sin of the people.

9.12.0.en: Moses was terrified at God's anger against his people and begged Him to forgive them, and God answered him. This shows the importance of intercession.

9.13.0.en: Because Aaron shared with the people in their error, in that he made the golden calf for them (Ex 32:21), the Lord was angry with him and decided to destroy him; but here too the Lord accepted the intercession of Moses and did not destroy Aaron.

9.14.1.en: The brook that descended out of the mount: the spring that came out of the rock which he struck at Rephidim (Ex 17:6). Moses took the golden image of the calf that they had made, burned it with fire, crushed it and ground it until it was as fine as dust, and then cast it into the brook that came down from the mountain in that place. The destruction of the calf is a declaration of the necessity of getting rid of sin and destroying it, and the people drank the water mixed with dust so that they would know that they had drunk iniquity like water.

9.15.0.en: Taberah: that is, burning; it is a place in the wilderness of Paran and the first place mentioned after their departure from Sinai (maps 4, 8).

9.15.1.en: Massah: that is, temptation; it is a place in the wilderness of Sin, also called Meribah (Ex 17:7), and it is near Rephidim, which is in the valley of Feiran.

9.15.2.en: Kibroth-hattaavah: that is, the graves of lust; it is a place north of Mount Horeb, in the south of the Sinai peninsula, and it is the place where the murmurers were buried.

9.15.3.en: Here Moses briefly mentions some other shameful incidents that took place on the part of the people during their long journey in the desert of Sinai.

9.15.4.en: At Taberah (Num 11:1-3) the people murmured and complained a great deal, so the Lord was angry and a fire was kindled among them and burned the outskirts of the place where they were staying; then Moses prayed to God and the fire was quenched. And at Massah (Ex 17:7), where the people quarreled with Moses over water, he said to them, "Why do ye tempt the LORD?" and he struck the rock, and water came out of it for the people to drink.

9.15.5.en: And at Kibroth-hattaavah (Num 11) the people murmured, saying, "Who shall give us flesh to eat?" Then a wind went forth from the Lord and brought quails from the sea and let them fall in the place where the people were encamped, and while the meat was still between their teeth the Lord struck them with a very great plague, and there they buried the people who had lusted for meat.

9.16.0.en: And at Kadesh-barnea, there they did not believe the Lord and did not listen to His voice when He asked them to get ready to possess the land, to arise and fight, because they were afraid of the words of the spies who had returned from spying out the land. They were unwilling to attack the inhabitants of the land, although God had reassured them, saying, "Fear not, neither be discouraged," and Moses said to them, "Dread not, neither be afraid of them." Then they sinned a second time when they decided to fight, while the Lord had said to them, "Go not up, neither fight."

9.17.0.en: Moses knew that they were a disobedient people from his constant companionship with them throughout the journey, and he cited as evidence the events, transgressions and errors that they had committed against the Lord since he took over their leadership, beginning with the Exodus from Egypt, and he confronted them with this judgment of his upon them.

9.17.1.en: It is good for you to remember your sins which you have confessed and which God has forgiven you, without going into their details, so that you may be humble before God and strive with zeal. Although God has forgiven you your sins, He awaits your love and your seriousness in spiritual striving, and this will make you have compassion on sinners, so that you do not judge them but support them with your love.

9.18.s.en: (3) The intercession of Moses for the people

9.18.0.en: Moses bowed down before the Lord forty days and forty nights to intercede for the people, so that the Lord would not destroy them, and he prayed to the Lord, asking Him to pardon the people and not to destroy them, because they were His people whom He had adopted and acquired for Himself and brought out of Egypt by His surpassing power.

9.19.0.en: Moses interceded by the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He asked the Lord to overlook the hardness of this people, their disobedience and their sin.

9.20.0.en: Moses prayed to the Lord, saying: May You, O Lord, pardon them, lest the rest of the nations gloat over them and justify the reason for Your destroying them as being Your inability to make them victorious over the peoples of the land that You promised them, and because You hated Your people You decided to wipe them out in the desert.

9.21.0.en: And Moses continues his prayer, saying that although the people have sinned, may You, O God, look upon them with a fatherly eye and pardon them, for they are Your people and Your children on whom You had compassion before, when they cried out to You from the humiliation of slavery, and You brought them out by Your mighty strength and Your great power.

9.21.1.en: God's tenderness is wonderful and surpasses all imagination. So humble yourself before Him with lowliness, and He will forgive you every sin and remove it from you; and intercede by His saints, and they will support you, and you will enjoy a fellowship of love with them and the work of God in you. God's love for His people and their fear of Him

10.0.0.en: God asked Moses to make two new tables of stone, because Moses had broken the first two, and to go up the mountain so that God might write on them the Ten Commandments, and then Moses was to place them in the ark of the covenant which God had commanded him to make.

10.1.0.en: Shittim wood: a kind of tree whose wood is heavy and hard and does not rot.

10.1.1.en: Moses carried out the Lord's instructions and made the ark of shittim wood, and hewed two tables of stone like the two he had broken before, as an expression of his anger at the people, and he went up the mountain with the two tables in his hand.

10.2.0.en: God wrote the Ten Commandments on the two new tables of stone, and they are the same commandments that He spoke on the day He appeared on the mountain in the form of fire before all the people (Ex 19:17).

10.3.0.en: Moses departed from before the Lord and came down from the mountain, and put the two tables in the ark of the covenant that Bezaleel made, before the rest of the contents of the tabernacle of meeting (Ex 25:10). There is another opinion, that Moses made a temporary wooden ark in which he put the two tables until the ark of the covenant and all the contents of the tabernacle were completed.

10.3.1.en: God in His love is ready to forgive your sins, to renew His covenants with you and to repeat His words to you so that you may live by them. So do not neglect His voice, but show your love, respond to Him and begin anew.

10.4.s.en: (2) The death of Aaron and the setting apart of the tribe of Levi

10.4.0.en: The wells of the children of Jaakan: the children of Jaakan are the name of a tribe descended from Seir, whose name was given to the place that lies 20 km to the northeast of Kadesh-barnea.

10.4.1.en: Mosera: perhaps it was the valley of Haroniyya; it lies south of Mount Hor and very close to it, and north of the wells of the children of Jaakan (map 16).

10.4.2.en: Map (16): a map showing the places mentioned in ch. 10, vv. 6, 7, which are:

10.4.3.en: The children of Jaakan, Mosera, Gudgodah, Jotbath; the locations of these places are not now determined with certainty, and they all lie in the region enclosed between the northern end of the Gulf of Aqaba and Mount Hor to the north.

10.4.4.en: Moses reminded them that during their journey in the desert, when they passed through the region of the wells of the children of Jaakan and reached the region of Mosera, which is next to Mount Hor, Aaron died there, and his son Eleazar succeeded him as head of the priesthood.

10.5.0.en: Gudgodah: a region north of the Gulf of Aqaba.

10.5.1.en: Jotbath: it is thought to be present-day Taba, 9 km southwest of the port of Eilat, on the western shore of the Red Sea.

10.5.2.en: After the death of Aaron at Mosera (Mount Hor), the people moved to two other places, Gudgodah and Jotbath, and the latter has many sources of water.

10.6.0.en: When they were in Sinai, and specifically at Horeb, they were given the details of the consecration of the tribe of Levi to the service of the tabernacle of meeting. The priesthood was limited to the sons of Aaron, while the Levites were assigned the following:

10.6.1.en: 1- Carrying the ark of the covenant, by the Kohathites, who are one of the clans of the Levites.

10.6.2.en: 2- To stand before the Lord to serve Him as assistants to the priests.

10.6.3.en: 3- Blessing God and praising His holy name in His house.

10.6.4.en: Although Levi had sinned with his brother Simeon in the incident of Shechem by killing the men of that tribe (Gen 34:30, 31), his descendants obeyed God, and their zeal appeared in helping Moses to kill the rebels who insisted on worshiping the golden calf (Ex 32:26-29), so God consecrated them to His service.

10.7.0.en: The Lord's instructions were that no portion of the land be allotted to the tribe of Levi when the land was divided among the tribes. This was because they were consecrated to the service of the Lord and had no time to spend on the worldly work needed for a livelihood; therefore the Lord assigned them a share of the burnt offerings, the sacrifices, the tithes, and the offerings and vows that the people offer to the Lord (Num: 11, 12), and in (ch. 14:27) the Lord says to the people, when they spend and eat, "And the Levite that is within thy gates (in your cities); thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee."

10.7.1.en: Also in (ch. 18:1, 2): "The priests the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi, shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel: they shall eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire, and his inheritance. Therefore shall they have no inheritance among their brethren: the LORD is their inheritance." So the meaning of the Lord being their inheritance is what is assigned to them of the fire offerings of the Lord and the offerings of the people.

10.7.2.en: If you are not consecrating all your time to God like the tribe of Levi, then at least consecrate your heart, that is, let your aim be clear, and it is God .. You do everything for Him and to please Him, and you repent of your sins that anger Him, so that you may be free to praise and glorify Him.

10.8.0.en: Here Moses returns to the main story that he recounted again in (vv. 1-5), the story of receiving the tables of the Law, and he says that he stayed on the mountain a second time forty days and forty nights, when the Lord accepted his intercession and pardoned the people.

10.9.0.en: Then the Lord commanded him to set out and to lead the people to enter and possess the land that He had promised to their fathers.

10.9.1.en: Pray to God for all who are distressed and those who are far away, however much they refuse God, for He wants the salvation of all and rejoices in your prayer for them.

10.10.s.en: (4) The fear of God and obedience to Him

10.10.0.en: After God showed His care and forgiveness for His people, He requires of them the following, so that they may continue to enjoy His care:

10.10.1.en: 1- The fear of God, which makes them keep away from the worship of idols and from every evil.

10.10.2.en: 2- Obedience to His commandments and orders that He declared to Moses.

10.10.3.en: 3- Love for Him, thanksgiving, and attachment to Him.

10.10.4.en: 4- Worship of Him according to what He made clear to Moses, with sacrifices, prayers and the various purifications.

10.11.0.en: Keeping the commandments and statutes is not a heavy burden that God places on His people, but is God's grace for the benefit and good of His people, for it gives them inner peace, success in their dealings and many blessings that they receive because of God's pleasure in them.

10.12.0.en: Moses shows the grace of God, the Creator of the heavens and the earth and all that is in them, how in His love He chose the people of Israel and distinguished them by His care for them because of the fathers' faith in Him and the readiness of the sons, their descendants, to obey Him.

10.13.0.en: Circumcise the foreskin of your heart: circumcision is the cutting of a part of a person's flesh, which God commanded as a symbol of cutting off sin and evil inclinations. The circumcision of the heart here is meant as purifying the heart from sin so that God may live. Be no more stiffnecked: stiffnecked means extreme stubbornness and resistance to God.

10.13.1.en: God requires of them to purify their hearts from evil and not to rebel and be stubborn with Him, but to obey His commandments.

10.14.0.en: Regardeth not persons: He shows favoritism to no one, even if he holds a position.

10.14.1.en: What shows that God deserves the obedience of His people is that He is above all gods, that is, everything that human beings consider gods and rulers; His power appeared in striking the gods of the Egyptians with the ten plagues and in His dividing the Red Sea, in addition to His justice, for He shows favoritism to no one as human beings do, nor does He pervert justice by taking a bribe, because He is perfect and in need of no one.

10.15.0.en: God is distinguished not only by being stronger than all the gods, but also by being merciful and caring for the weak, such as the widow, the fatherless and the stranger, and giving them their rights and tending them.

10.16.0.en: The tender God calls them to show kindness to strangers, remembering that they were strangers in the land of Egypt, that is, to feel for strangers and have compassion on them.

10.16.1.en: May you care for the weak of every kind, whether the poor, the sick or anyone who suffers weakness in his personality, so that you respect everyone and support and encourage them, remembering God's tenderness and mercy toward your own weakness.

10.17.0.en: Israel must fear God and offer Him the worship that is fitting, cleave to the Lord and continue in communion with Him, and not let the name of another god come to his tongue when he swears.

10.18.0.en: Great and terrible things: the ten plagues that terrified the Egyptians.

10.18.1.en: And he must take pride in the Lord, for He is the One who performed the glorious saving works to bring him out of slavery, of which the people were eyewitnesses.

10.19.0.en: And God fulfilled His promise to Abraham to make his descendants as many as the stars of heaven, whereas they were a small number of people, not exceeding seventy souls, when Jacob and his sons, the fathers of the tribes, came to Egypt in the days of Joseph's rule.

10.19.1.en: Review your life from time to time to know how much good the Lord has done for you, more than you ask or think, so that you may live a life of evil and constant joy.

10.19.2.en: The recompense for obeying the commandment and for disobeying it
